objects.original: Two normalized restricted-Gaussian fibers with centers y and yprime share the normalizer base nu; relative Fisher information is integrated under the left probability fiber mu_y.
objects.reconstructed: The Lean theorem has separate measures nu and mu: nu occurs only in the two logarithmic normalizers, while RelativeFisher.information integrates the explicit representative under mu.
objects.evidence: The signature is (nu mu : Measure State) [IsProbabilityMeasure mu]; every normalizer integral is with respect to nu, and the first argument of RelativeFisher.information is mu.

domains.original: Finite-dimensional Euclidean space R^d, positive fiber variance eta, and normalized restricted-Gaussian fibers.
domains.reconstructed: State is EuclideanSpace real iota with Fintype iota; eta is a nonzero real; nu is any measure and mu is any probability measure.
domains.evidence: EuclideanSpace real iota with Fintype iota is the coordinate finite-dimensional source domain. The broader eta and measure hypotheses are accounted for in the assumptions and quantifiers slots.

quantifiers.original: For every pair of centers y and yprime for the two fibers obtained from the common base nu.
quantifiers.reconstructed: For every finite index type, every nu, every probability mu, every nonzero eta, and all centers y and yprime.
quantifiers.evidence: The Lean identity is universal in the probability integration law mu rather than only the source choice mu = left tilt of nu; this is valid because the score is spatially constant.

assumptions.original: eta is positive; the fibers are normalized from a common base nu; the expectation law is the left probability fiber.
assumptions.reconstructed: eta is merely nonzero; mu is required only to be a probability measure; no equality between mu and a tilt of nu and no integrability or positivity condition on the nu-normalizers is assumed.
assumptions.evidence: The proof uses nu-normalizers only as constants under spatial differentiation and uses IsProbabilityMeasure mu only to integrate the resulting constant. The source specialization is obtained by setting mu to the normalized left fiber and using eta > 0 to obtain eta != 0.

conclusion.original: The relative Fisher energy of the explicit quadratic log-ratio representative is eta^(-2) times norm(y-yprime)^2.
conclusion.reconstructed: RelativeFisher.information mu 1 r equals (eta^(-1))^2 times norm(y-yprime)^2.
conclusion.evidence: The embedded proof substitutes gradient r = eta^(-1) smul (y-yprime), integrates its constant squared norm under a probability law, and squares the scalar; (eta^(-1))^2 is exactly eta^(-2) for eta != 0.

scopes.original: Only the explicit smooth-representative Fisher evaluation is selected; fiber construction, canonical llr differentiation, LSI, Talagrand T2, and Wasserstein contraction are excluded.
scopes.reconstructed: The declaration concludes only an equality for RelativeFisher.information applied to the displayed explicit function and invokes the previously proved explicit-representative gradient theorem.
scopes.evidence: Neither the theorem statement nor proof identifies the function with a canonical llr or states any log-Sobolev, T2, or W2 proposition. The module documentation explicitly preserves these exclusions.

constant_dependencies.original: The value depends exactly on eta through eta^(-2) and on the centers through norm(y-yprime)^2, with no dimension or base-measure factor.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: The right side is (eta^(-1))^2 * norm(y-yprime)^2 and is independent of nu, mu, and the finite dimension.
constant_dependencies.evidence: The signs in the representative give gradient eta^(-1)(y-yprime), not its negative; squaring yields the exact eta^(-2) coefficient and removes no additional constants.

deltas.description: Lean quantifies over any probability integration law mu independent of the common normalizer base nu. The cited left-fiber case is a direct specialization, and the proof genuinely needs only total mass one after the constant-score rewrite.
Lean weakens the paper assumption eta > 0 to eta != 0. The gradient and squared-energy identity are algebraically valid on this larger domain, while the source specialization remains available.

review_evidence: Fresh module-binding review used only reviewer-v4.json. The sole implementation change is a private reducible State abbreviation for EuclideanSpace; the public mathematical body, proof, lesson and source binding are otherwise unchanged. The module separates nu from mu, yields score eta^(-1)(y-yprime) and exact eta^(-2) squared-distance Fisher energy, admits the source left-fiber specialization, and makes no canonical-llr, LSI, T2 or Wasserstein claim.
